questions.stem: A sequence is defined by t₁ = 7 and tₙ₊₁ = tₙ − 3. What are its first four terms?
questions.explanation: Each term is 3 less than the one before: 7, 4, 1, −2. The list starting at 4 leaves out the first term, t₁ = 7.

questions.stem: Which rule gives the general term of the arithmetic sequence 5, 11, 17, 23, ...?
questions.explanation: With t₁ = 5 and d = 6, tₙ = 5 + (n − 1)6 = 6n − 1. The rule 6n + 5 gives t₁ = 11, one term too far along.

questions.stem: What is the 20th term of the arithmetic sequence 5, 11, 17, ...?
questions.explanation: tₙ = a + (n − 1)d, so t₂₀ = 5 + 19 × 6 = 119. Using 20 steps instead of 19 gives 125.

questions.stem: Which term of the arithmetic sequence 8, 14, 20, ... equals 200?
questions.explanation: Solve 8 + (n − 1)6 = 200: (n − 1)6 = 192, so n − 1 = 32 and n = 33. Stopping at n − 1 = 32 gives the 32nd term by mistake.

questions.stem: In an arithmetic sequence, t₄ = 19 and t₁₀ = 43. What are the first term and the common difference?
questions.explanation: From t₄ to t₁₀ is 6 steps, so 6d = 43 − 19 = 24 and d = 4. Then t₁ = 19 − 3 × 4 = 7. Subtracting 4 × 4 from 19 gives 3, one step too many.

questions.stem: The terms of an arithmetic sequence are plotted as points (n, tₙ). The points:
options: lie on a parabola whose turning point is the first term
lie on a straight line whose gradient is the common difference
lie on an exponential curve whose base is the common difference
lie on a straight line whose gradient is the first term
questions.explanation: tₙ = a + (n − 1)d = dn + (a − d) is a linear function of n, so the points are on a line with gradient d. This linear nature is why arithmetic sequences model steady, discrete growth or decay.

questions.stem: $5000 is invested at 4% per annum simple interest. The values at the end of each year form an arithmetic sequence. What is the value at the end of 6 years?
questions.explanation: Simple interest adds 4% of $5000, which is $200, every year, so after 6 years the value is 5000 + 6 × 200 = $6200. The value $6326.60 compounds the interest instead.

questions.stem: $5000 is invested at 4% per annum simple interest. Which recurrence relation gives the value Vₙ after n years?
questions.explanation: Simple interest adds the same amount, 0.04 × 5000 = $200, each year, which is an arithmetic sequence. Multiplying by 1.04 each year would be compound interest.

questions.stem: A club has 120 members and gains 15 members each month. After how many months will it first have 300 members?
questions.explanation: The membership after n months is the arithmetic sequence 120 + 15n, and 120 + 15n = 300 gives 15n = 180, so n = 12. The value 20 divides 300 by 15 and ignores the starting 120 members.

questions.stem: What is the sum 1 + 2 + 3 + ... + 100?
questions.explanation: Using Sₙ = n(a + l)/2, the sum is 100(1 + 100)/2 = 5050. The value 10 100 forgets to halve, since each pair of terms is counted twice when the sum is written forwards and backwards.

questions.stem: What is the sum of the first 20 terms of the arithmetic sequence 5, 11, 17, ...?
questions.explanation: Sₙ = (n/2)(2a + (n − 1)d) = 10(10 + 19 × 6) = 10 × 124 = 1240. The value 2480 leaves out the factor 1/2.

questions.stem: Evaluate the arithmetic series 3 + 7 + 11 + ... + 99.
questions.explanation: The number of terms is (99 − 3)/4 + 1 = 25, so the sum is 25(3 + 99)/2 = 1275. Forgetting the + 1 gives 24 terms and a sum of 1224.

questions.stem: The formula for the sum of an arithmetic sequence is found by writing Sₙ forwards and then backwards and adding the two lines. Why does this work?
options: The terms double each time, so the two lines cancel out
The middle term is always the mean of the first and the last
Each pair of matching terms adds to the same total, a + l
Each term appears once in the sum, so the total is n times a
questions.explanation: Going forwards the terms rise by d and going backwards they fall by d, so every matching pair adds to a + l. There are n pairs, so 2Sₙ = n(a + l) and Sₙ = n(a + l)/2.

questions.stem: How many terms of the series 2 + 5 + 8 + ... must be added to give a sum of 155?
questions.explanation: With a = 2 and d = 3, Sₙ = (n/2)(4 + 3(n − 1)) = n(3n + 1)/2. Setting this to 155 gives 3n² + n − 310 = 0, so (n − 10)(3n + 31) = 0 and n = 10, the positive whole-number solution.

questions.stem: A theatre has 15 rows. The front row has 20 seats and each row has 2 more seats than the row in front. How many seats are there in total?
questions.explanation: The last row has 20 + 14 × 2 = 48 seats, so the total is 15(20 + 48)/2 = 510. The value 525 uses 15 × 2 for the last row's extra seats instead of 14 × 2.

questions.stem: The sum of the first n terms of an arithmetic sequence is Sₙ = n² + 4n. What is the 10th term?
questions.explanation: The 10th term is the sum of 10 terms minus the sum of 9 terms: S₁₀ − S₉ = 140 − 117 = 23. The value 140 is the sum of the first 10 terms, not the 10th term.

questions.stem: A sequence is defined by t₁ = 3 and tₙ₊₁ = 2tₙ. What are its first four terms?
questions.explanation: Each term is double the one before, so the terms are 3, 6, 12, 24. The list 3, 6, 9, 12 adds 3 each time, which is arithmetic.

questions.stem: What is the common ratio of the geometric sequence 48, −24, 12, −6, ...?
questions.explanation: The ratio is −24/48 = −1/2, and each later term is also −1/2 times the one before. The value −24 is the difference between the first two terms, not the ratio.

questions.stem: Which rule gives the general term of the geometric sequence 2, 6, 18, 54, ...?
questions.explanation: With a = 2 and r = 3, tₙ = arⁿ⁻¹ = 2 × 3ⁿ⁻¹. The rule 2 × 3ⁿ gives t₁ = 6, one term too far along.

questions.stem: What is the 8th term of the geometric sequence 2, 6, 18, ...?
questions.explanation: t₈ = 2 × 3⁷ = 2 × 2187 = 4374. Using 3⁸ gives 13 122, and 46 is the 8th term of an arithmetic sequence with difference 4.

questions.stem: In a geometric sequence with positive terms, t₃ = 12 and t₆ = 96. What are the first term and the common ratio?
questions.explanation: From t₃ to t₆ is three steps, so r³ = 96/12 = 8 and r = 2. Then t₁ = 12/2² = 3. The value r = 8 forgets that three steps multiply by r³.

questions.stem: The terms of a geometric sequence with first term 5 and common ratio 1.2 are plotted as points (n, tₙ). The points lie on:
questions.explanation: tₙ = 5 × 1.2ⁿ⁻¹ is an exponential function of n, so the points lie on an exponential curve. Points on a straight line belong to an arithmetic sequence.

questions.stem: A geometric sequence has first term 50 and common ratio 0.8. As n → ∞, the terms:
questions.explanation: Each term is 80% of the one before, and 0.8ⁿ⁻¹ → 0 as n grows, so the terms approach 0. They never reach it, but they get as close as you like.

questions.stem: A geometric sequence has first term 2 and common ratio −1.5. How do the terms behave as n → ∞?
options: They alternate in sign and grow in size without bound
They alternate in sign and approach 0
They are all positive and grow without bound
questions.explanation: A negative ratio makes the signs alternate, and since 1.5 > 1 the size of the terms grows each time. A ratio between −1 and 0 would alternate and approach 0.

questions.stem: For which values of the common ratio r do the terms of a geometric sequence (first term not 0) approach 0 as n → ∞?
questions.explanation: The terms approach 0 exactly when |r| < 1, including negative ratios such as −0.5, whose terms alternate in sign while shrinking. The condition r < 1 would include r = −2, whose terms grow.

questions.stem: A geometric sequence has first term 4 and common ratio −1. How do the terms behave as n → ∞?
questions.explanation: Multiplying by −1 just changes the sign, so the terms are 4, −4, 4, −4, ... and never settle on a limit. Only ratios strictly between −1 and 1 give terms that approach 0.

questions.stem: What is the sum of the first 8 terms of 3 + 6 + 12 + ...?
questions.explanation: Sₙ = a(rⁿ − 1)/(r − 1) = 3(2⁸ − 1)/1 = 3 × 255 = 765. The value 384 is the 8th term, 3 × 2⁷, not the sum.

questions.stem: What is the sum of the first 6 terms of 1 + 1/2 + 1/4 + ...?
questions.explanation: Sₙ = a(1 − rⁿ)/(1 − r) = (1 − 1/64)/(1/2) = (63/64) × 2 = 63/32. The value 31/16 is the sum of only 5 terms, and 2 is the limit the sums approach.

questions.stem: Monthly deposits into a savings plan start at $100 and each deposit is 5% more than the one before. What is the total of the first 12 deposits, to the nearest dollar?
questions.explanation: The deposits form a geometric sequence with a = 100 and r = 1.05, so S₁₂ = 100(1.05¹² − 1)/0.05 ≈ $1592. The value $1260 adds 5% of $100 each month, which is arithmetic growth.

questions.stem: Which of these sequences is geometric?
questions.explanation: In 3, −6, 12, −24 each term is −2 times the one before. The sequence 3, 6, 9, 12 is arithmetic, and the other two have neither a common difference nor a common ratio.

questions.stem: $5000 is invested at 4% per annum, compounded annually. What is the value after 3 years?
questions.explanation: Compound interest multiplies by 1.04 each year, so the value is 5000 × 1.04³ = $5624.32. The value $5600 is simple interest, adding $200 each year.

questions.stem: $5000 is invested at 4% per annum, compounded annually. Which recurrence relation gives the value Vₙ after n years?
questions.explanation: Each year the value is multiplied by 1 + 0.04 = 1.04, giving a geometric sequence. Multiplying by 0.04 would give only the interest, not the new balance.

questions.stem: $5000 is invested for 10 years at 4% per annum. How much more does compound interest (compounded annually) earn than simple interest, to the nearest dollar?
questions.explanation: Simple interest gives 5000 + 10 × 200 = $7000, while compound interest gives 5000 × 1.04¹⁰ ≈ $7401. The difference is about $401. The value $2401 is the compound interest earned, not the difference.

questions.stem: A car bought for $30 000 loses 15% of its value each year. What is its value after 4 years, to the nearest dollar?
questions.explanation: Each year the value is multiplied by 0.85, so after 4 years it is 30 000 × 0.85⁴ ≈ $15 660. Taking 15% of $30 000 off four times gives $12 000, which is linear decay.

questions.stem: A ball is dropped from 10 m and each bounce reaches 60% of the previous height. How high does it reach after the third bounce?
questions.explanation: The heights form a geometric sequence: 10 × 0.6 = 6, then 3.6, then 2.16 m after the third bounce. The value 1.296 m is after the fourth bounce.

questions.stem: The geometric sequence 5, 10, 20, ... continues. Which is the first term greater than 1000?
questions.explanation: tₙ = 5 × 2ⁿ⁻¹. The 8th term is 5 × 2⁷ = 640, below 1000, and the 9th term is 5 × 2⁸ = 1280, the first above it.
